non_goals: Proving any project leak-free. A benchmark can only show which known leak patterns are detected.
Replacing code review. The detectors are a floor, not a certificate.
risks: The corpus holds one example of each leak on one dataset and one model; detection could differ on other code shapes.
Score inflation is measured on a single split, so small inflations are within run-to-run noise.
The portfolio snapshot reflects artifacts at the moment this project was trained, not live state.
lessons: An auditor that has never been tested against planted leaks proves nothing by passing.
The costliest missed leak was a feature built from the label with noise added, which no correlation threshold near one can catch.
Name-based static rules miss the same leak once a variable is renamed.
Some leaks lower a score rather than raise it, so inflation alone is not a safe proxy for whether a leak exists.
A passing audit in this portfolio rules out split mistakes and blatant label leaks; the subtler cases are guarded by design, not by the auditor.
references: Kaufman, S., Rosset, S., Perlich, C., & Stitelman, O. (2012). Leakage in data mining: Formulation, detection, and avoidance. ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data, 6(4).
Kapoor, S., & Narayanan, A. (2023). Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science. Patterns, 4(9).
Jia, Y., & Harman, M. (2011). An analysis and survey of the development of mutation testing. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, 37(5), 649–678.
Brodersen, K. H., Ong, C. S., Stephan, K. E., & Buhmann, J. M. (2010). The balanced accuracy and its posterior distribution. International Conference on Pattern Recognition.
